newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Eximbank plans Euro and Samurai bond issues.
newsitem.headline: Turk Eximbank plans Euro and Samurai bond issues.

text.p: Turkey's state-run Export-Import Bank is planning to issue bonds in Japanese and European markets, its general manager said.
"We will issue bonds in the Japanese and European markets within two or three months," Can Yesilada, general manager of the bank, told Reuters.
Yesilada said the bonds would be issued without any guarantee from the Turkish treasury.
Turk Eximbank signed an accord with a 19-bank consortium on Friday for a $100-million syndicated loan accord.
The consortium included ABN Amro, Citibank, Credit Lyonnais, The Sakura Bank, The Sanwa Bank and Societe Generale.
The one-year loan carries an interest rate of LIBOR plus 75 basis points.
Yesilada said the bank aimed to borrow more abroad.
"Domestic debts make up 80 percent of the total debt. But we aim to equalise both sides of the total debt," he added.
In 1996, the bank financed 23 percent of Turkey's total exports which stood at $22 billion.
"Our target is to finance the same portion of the increasing exports in 1997 and we need more money to do this," Yesilada said.
